::: {#exr-top-k-count}
#### Counting values with few larger-or-equal values

Let $t_1, \ldots, t_N$ be real numbers, and for each $j$ let $N_j$ be the number of $i$ with $t_i \ge t_j$ (including $i = j$).
Show that for every integer $k \ge 0$, at most $k$ of the $N_j$ are at most $k$:

$$\sum_{j=1}^N \indic{N_j \le k} \le k.$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#sol-top-k-count}

List the values in decreasing order, breaking ties arbitrarily, so that $t_{[1]} \ge t_{[2]} \ge \cdots \ge t_{[N]}$.
Suppose the value $t_{[r]}$ at position $r > k$ has $N_j \le k$, where $j$ is its original index.
Then the $r$ values at positions $1, \ldots, r$ are all at least $t_{[r]}$,
so $N_j \ge r > k$, which contradicts $N_j \le k$.
So every $j$ with $N_j \le k$ sits at a position $r \le k$ of the sorted list.
That list has $k$ such positions, and each belongs to one index, so at most $k$ indices have $N_j \le k$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#lem-top-k-count}
#### At most $k$ values have $k$ or fewer values at least as large

Let $t_1, \ldots, t_N$ be real numbers,
and for each $j$ let $N_j$ be the number of indices $i$ with $t_i \ge t_j$ (including $i = j$).
Then for every integer $k \ge 0$, at most $k$ of the $N_j$ are at most $k$:

$$\sum_{j=1}^N \indic{N_j \le k} \le k,$$

where $\indic{A}$ is $1$ if $A$ is true and $0$ otherwise.

:::

::: proof
This is the solution to @exr-top-k-count, worked in @sol-top-k-count.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exr-relabeling-count}
#### Relabeling the data permutes the relabelings

For a permutation $\sigma$ define $N_\sigma(y)$, the number of relabelings at least as extreme as $y_\sigma$:

$$N_\sigma(y) \eqdef \sum_{\pi \in S_n} \indic{T(y_\pi) \ge T(y_\sigma)}.$$

Write $\iota$ for the identity permutation, so $N_\iota(y)$ is $n!$ times the permutation p-value of @def-permutation-p-value.
Express $N_\sigma(y)$ in terms of $N_\iota$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#sol-relabeling-count}

The entries of $(y_\sigma)_{\pi'}$ are $y_{\sigma(\pi'(i))}$, so $(y_\sigma)_{\pi'} = y_{\sigma \circ \pi'}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
N_\iota(y_\sigma)
&= \sum_{\pi' \in S_n} \indic{T\paren{(y_\sigma)_{\pi'}} \ge T(y_\sigma)}
&& \text{(definition, with $y_\sigma$ in place of $y$)}\\
&= \sum_{\pi' \in S_n} \indic{T\paren{y_{\sigma \circ \pi'}} \ge T(y_\sigma)}
&& \text{($(y_\sigma)_{\pi'} = y_{\sigma \circ \pi'}$)}\\
&= \sum_{\pi \in S_n} \indic{T(y_\pi) \ge T(y_\sigma)}
&& \text{($\pi = \sigma \circ \pi'$ is a bijection of $S_n$)}\\
&= N_\sigma(y)
&& \text{(definition)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So $N_\sigma(y) = N_\iota(y_\sigma)$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#lem-relabeling-count}
#### Relabeling the data permutes the relabelings

Let $T$ be a statistic, let $y = (\outvar_1, \ldots, \outvar_n)$ be data,
let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$,
and let $y_\sigma$ be $y$ with its entries relabeled by $\sigma \in S_n$.
For $\sigma \in S_n$ let $N_\sigma(y) \eqdef \sum_{\pi \in S_n} \indic{T(y_\pi) \ge T(y_\sigma)}$
be the number of relabelings at least as extreme as $y_\sigma$,
and write $\iota$ for the identity permutation,
so that $N_\iota(y)$ is $n!$ times the [permutation p-value](#def-permutation-p-value) of $T(y)$.
Then relabeling the data by $\sigma$ turns $N_\iota$ into $N_\sigma$:

$$N_\sigma(y) = N_\iota(y_\sigma).$$

:::

::: proof
This is the solution to @exr-relabeling-count, worked in @sol-relabeling-count.
:::
